author: EmuCore - Hub
title: I Interfaced to a Secret UART Port on The PlayStation 2 Emotion Engine Chip - PS2 Development [#72]
summary: Behind The Code with Gerry reconstructs a PC interface to the undocumented RS-232 UART on the PS2 Emotion Engine, combining service documentation, transceiver electronics and homebrew debugging history in a physical engineering project.

blocks.text: The project starts from Joe Grand’s 2004 writing and asks whether a modern Windows PC can communicate through a serial port hidden around the Emotion Engine. The description identifies an SCPH-39001 console, the relevant service manual, a MAX3323 transceiver and teardown material, then places the interface in the context of PS2 homebrew development and debugging. This makes the video unusually concrete: it is about voltage translation, board access and a specific diagnostic path, not merely a software menu labelled serial output.

Opening and wiring vintage hardware can damage the console, and undocumented pads may differ across motherboard revisions. The public notes link useful sources but provide neither a validated schematic package, signal-voltage table nor compatibility matrix for other PS2 models. A successful PC connection also does not make the port a full replacement for an official development kit. The entry documents an engineering investigation; replication requires service-manual verification, electrical measurement and appropriate hardware safety practices.
